WHY FIVE IDEAS. Five is everything that cleared the bar — no padding, no trimming for a tidy count, and no horizon balancing. Recomputed ratios from the final levels: NEE 30.50/10.50 = 2.90 against a 2.5 long-term floor; CVS 33.45/13.00 = 2.57 against 2.5; AMRC 7.70/3.00 = 2.57 against 2.0; XLU 3.30/1.50 = 2.20 against 2.0. Stop distances in ATRs: AMRC 2.10 (stock floor 2.0, under the 2.5 comfort level), XLU 2.47 (ETF floor 1.8). Two ideas carry no stop by design, because they are long-term theses with bear-case prices instead: CVS $66, NEE $70.

BE SUSPICIOUS OF CVS's 2.57. It clears the long-term floor by 0.07, and the whole margin lives in the bear case, which is the softest number on the page: at a $66 bear case the ratio is 2.57, at $70 it is 3.72, and at $62 it is 1.97 and fails. The $66 is defended (roughly 8.2x a flat, no-growth $8.00, below the 52-week low of 69.51) but it is a judgement, not a measurement. CVS and AMRC both landing on 2.57 is coincidence — they are measured against different floors and derived from unrelated methods (a 13x multiple on a guided EPS floor; a 50% retracement of a 150-day decline). XLU's 2.20 is not a fresh calculation at all: those are the unchanged levels of a position opened 2026-11-02.

HII WILL PROBABLY FAIL MECHANICAL VALIDATION, AND THE IDEA IS STILL RIGHT. This is a stop being added to a filled winner: the position was bought at 262.00 on 2026-10-12 and trades at 303.99, +21.0%, with no stop at all. The new 278.00 stop is 2.37 ATR below the LIVE price and sits just under both the SMA20 (281.68) and SMA50 (279.05) — but it is 16.00 points ABOVE the entry of record, so validate_report.py's direction check ('downside must be below entry for a buy') and its stop-distance check (which measures from entry, giving 1.46 ATR) will both read FAIL, and phase 2d will likely demote the row to the watchlist. Both failures are artifacts of measuring a profit-protecting stop against a fill the position left 16% ago; the stop reduces this position's risk rather than inflating its ratio, which is the abuse those checks exist to catch. `risk_reward` is published as null rather than as the 4.86 the arithmetic yields, because that number is meaningless, and the expectancy figures the validator computes for HII are not comparable with the other four for the same reason. The entry is left at the truth — 262.00 — because a filled position can have its exits amended but never its entry. IF HII IS DEMOTED, STILL ENTER THE 278.00 STOP WITH THE BROKER: that instruction is the entire content of the recommendation.

NKE CANNOT BE CLOSED THROUGH THIS SCHEMA. Research decided to close the 2026-09-08 NKE short at the market today rather than wait to be stopped at 41.00 (0.51 away, 0.47 ATR), because the thesis was consumer weakness and the post-election discretionary bid invalidated it. There is no field for an early close, and publishing a close as a short recommendation would read as 'short NKE here', which is the opposite of the instruction. It is on the watchlist as an explicit manual close. LULU needs no such handling: its 112.00 stop is genuinely through on the 112.06 close, so grading closes it. The falsification pass cuts against both closures and is recorded honestly — the tariff-relief premise behind the squeeze does not survive, which makes both better shorts today than they were on Tuesday; they are on the watchlist as conditional re-shorts (NKE below its SMA20 of 37.29, LULU below its SMA50 of 102.34) rather than re-pitched into day one of a squeeze.

CORRELATION IS AT THE CAP, DELIBERATELY. Three of five ideas depend on the post-election energy-and-power policy reprice: XLU, NEE and AMRC. That is the cap of 3, counted honestly rather than conveniently. Two mitigations rather than assumptions: XLU is an existing position being held, not new risk, and NEE and AMRC are both wait-flagged limits below the market, so the three are not three simultaneous entries. CVS (a company-specific valuation case off its own earnings) and HII (a stop amendment) are independent.

TWO MECHANICAL FLAGS CHECKED AT SYNTHESIS, BOTH ARTIFACTS, NEITHER SUPPRESSED. A dry run of validate_report.py was used to find surprises while they could still be investigated, and it surfaced two failures on AMRC that are worth labelling before the red team reads them.
  (1) AMRC's bid/ask reads 18.94 x 30.39, a 46.42% spread, which will FAIL the spread check. That is not a market: the depth quote comes back `is_real_time: false` stamped 'Nov 4, 2026' on a stock that closed at 21.25 and trades $11.53M a day, so it is an unusable pre-open book rather than a real cost of trading. The other four names quoted sanely at the same moment (NEE 0.55%, CVS 1.33%, HII 2.18%, XLU no book outside hours). The honest caveat survives the artifact, though: AMRC is the one small cap here, its entry is a limit placed four sessions out after the 2026-11-09 print, and the spread that will actually be paid is the regular-session one — re-check it at entry and never send this order at market.
  (2) AMRC's earnings catalyst reads as unverifiable ('not on the fetched calendar'), and that is a truncation artifact, not a wrong date. market_data.py earnings caps its response at 1500 rows, so a 45-day fetch never reaches 2026-11-09. A 7-day fetch confirms AMRC 2026-11-09 amc, EPS estimate 0.5426 on revenue of $584.35M — exactly the research figures. Every other date in this report was re-confirmed against that same fetch at synthesis: VST 2026-11-06 bmo, MRNA 2026-11-06 bmo, OXY 2026-11-09 amc, ONON 2026-11-10 bmo.
Separately, source verification could not reach 3 of 4 NEE sources and 2 of 4 CVS sources — SEC, Fool and GuruFocus bot-block the checker. Those documents were read during research and the inability to re-fetch them from CI is not evidence against them; no source returned a 404.

RED TEAM (phase 2c). Four ideas survive, one instruction moved, and the ranking recomputed by the strategy file's rule — conviction first, then reward-to-risk: NEE 1, AMRC 2, CVS 3, XLU 4. AMRC ranks above CVS because conviction leads the sort, not because a 1.5% small cap is a better use of capital than a 3% core holding.
CVS DOWNGRADED to conviction 3 and trimmed from 4% to 3%. The 4 was paid for with three evidence kinds and `counter_argument_answered` is not one of them here: that entry answers Health Services erosion, while this report's own `key_risk` names a statutory change to PBM rebate economics as the risk no operating beat answers — the strongest case against is stated, not answered. Two kinds hold, which is a 3, and a conviction-3 single name belongs in the 2-3% standard tier. The thesis survives: the beat, the raise, the $8.65 2027 floor and the split are all read from primary documents. Two specifics were sloppy and are fixed. The catalyst claimed the 2027 floor was '+13%' where 8.65 against the raised FY26 'at least $8.20' is +5.5%; management's 13% is measured off a lower base and the field now says so. And the 112.45 target is 13x against a stock at 9.25x, so almost all of the return is a multiple re-rating — at an unchanged 9.25x the 2027 floor is worth about $80, which is today's price. Recorded rather than resolved: research listed two candidate explanations for the 12.5% fall and settled neither, and the report asserts the political one. That is the same standard of established cause that kept MRNA out of the report.
HII MOVED TO THE WATCHLIST WITH THE 278.00 STOP INTACT, and this is not a kill. The schema cannot express a profit-protecting stop above the fill of record, so 2d's demotion was certain and would have published a note reading as a rejection for a stop too tight. That is not a market and not a cost of trading; if 2d demotes AMRC on it, the conditional stands exactly as written — wait for the print, limit only, never market, re-check the spread in the regular session. market_context.summary: One driver owned the tape: the 2026-11-03 midterms delivered Democratic majorities in BOTH chambers, including the Texas governor's race, and 2026-11-04 repriced five sectors at once. Merchant/IPP power generators were crushed on data-center moratorium risk (VST -13.8% to 120.29, NRG -13.5%, GEV -9.3%, TLN -8.5%, CEG -6.7%) while rate-regulated utilities were flat to higher (XLU +0.44%) — that split is the cleanest available read that this was a merchant-power POLICY event, not a power-demand event. Hyperscalers went the other way the same session (MSFT +6.68% to a record 555.80, AMZN +6%), so the tape did not de-rate AI capex, it de-rated the permission to build generation. Energy sold off hard (USO -8.1%, XOP -6.4%, XLE -4.7%, OXY -5.1%), defence fell (HII -4.1%, RTX -2.6%), steel fell on tariff-rollback hope (STLD -3.0%), gold ripped (GLD +3.7%) on a fiscal-expansion bid, and discretionary importers squeezed (NKE +5.2%, LULU +4.8%, ONON +5.8%). The index closed up hard — reporting puts the Dow +1,569 points, +3%, at 53,356.12 — but gold and bonds rose with it and two sectors collapsed, so this is dispersion, not clean risk-on. The most important piece of work this run was a falsification: the obvious 'Democratic sweep = tariff rollback' trade does not survive, because a rollback faces a presidential veto with no supermajority in either chamber, and Bloomberg's own sector work expects continued tariff pressure on importers into 2027. Rates are a steepening/term-premium tape rather than a growth-scare one: US10Y 4.95% against 3.88% fed funds, 10y-2y +0.32. Most of today's value is in NOT chasing the reprice — two shorts closed, two stale entries withdrawn, one unprotected 21% winner finally given a stop.

recommendations.thesis: NextEra is the only large US company that is simultaneously the biggest regulated utility (FPL) and the biggest renewables developer, which makes it the one name that gains from both halves of the 2026-11-04 repricing rather than one: a Democratic Congress is the most favourable policy regime renewables have had, and the same session that bid NEE +4.89% took merchant power down 7 to 14 points (VST -13.8%, NRG -13.5%, CEG -6.7%) on state-level data-center permitting hostility. Power demand does not go away because a statehouse blocked a gas plant, and the supply that remains politically buildable is disproportionately NextEra backlog. The recommendation is explicitly a limit below the market, because at 88.45 the valuation does not clear the floor and the only way to make it clear would be to raise the target.
recommendations.key_risk: The 8% compounding guide runs through 2032 and the Dominion combination does not close until H2 2027, so this thesis is carried for years on management execution — and with the 10-year at 4.95% every gigawatt of that 36.7 GW backlog costs more to finance, which is where a debt-funded utility growth plan breaks first. Invalidation: the 8%+ adjusted EPS growth guide through 2032 cut or withdrawn, the Dominion combination abandoned or repriced, or the 36.7 GW backlog shrinking for two consecutive quarters.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is that the entry never fills: NEE is 9.4% above its own 20-day mean after a policy move, leadership tends to persist, and a limit at 80.50 may simply watch the stock leave. That is accepted deliberately — buying at 88.45 gives 1.22 against a 2.5 floor, so the choice is a limit that may not fill or a trade that does not qualify. Second count against: six-month relative return is still -7.28% versus SPY +4.49%, so one month of leadership is being extrapolated from a de-rating base. Red team, third count against: this is not an independent exposure from the XLU position ranked below it. NEE is XLU's largest single holding at roughly 12.7% of the fund as of October 2026, so the 3% XLU hold is already partly this trade, and both ideas name the same 4.95% 10-year as their key risk. If the 80.50 limit fills while XLU is held, that is 7% of capital on one duration bet in regulated utilities — take the pair as one exposure rather than two.

evidence.detail: Q3 2026 results: adjusted EPS $1.24 against $1.1917 consensus, up $0.11 and 9.7% y/y with adjusted earnings up $244M; nine-month adjusted EPS +9.5%; renewables backlog 36.7 GW. FY26 adjusted EPS guidance held at $3.92-$4.02 with management targeting the high end despite an expected weaker Q4 wind resource, and the 8%-or-better annual adjusted EPS growth rate through 2032 off the 2025 base of $3.71 reaffirmed, with operating cash flow growth at or above it.

2029 adjusted EPS on the company's own reaffirmed 8% compounding off the $3.71 2025 base = 3.71 x 1.08^4 = $5.05. At 22x — below NEE's peak multiple, a premium justified by a regulated earnings base plus the largest US renewables development arm — that is $111. Bear case prices a missed guide: 4% compounding gives 2029 EPS of $4.34 and the multiple compresses to a plain-utility 16x = $70, below the 150-day low of 74.41. From the 80.50 entry that is 30.50/10.50 = 2.90 against the 2.5 floor; from 88.45 it is 1.22 and fails, which is why the entry is a limit.

The 78.50-81.50 entry zone is the SMA50 at 80.3526 and SMA20 at 80.853, which NEE traded at four sessions ago before running 82.14 to 88.45. ATR14 is 1.8989 (2.15%), so the zone is roughly 4 ATR below the close rather than a reflex discount, and the $70 bear case sits below the 150-day low of 74.41. Average dollar volume $1.17B a day.

Computed relative strength: NEE +13.57% over one month against SPY -1.58% (+15.15pp) and against sector peer XLU +5.95% (+7.62pp), so this is leadership rather than a laggard being caught — while a six-month return of -7.28% versus SPY +4.49% shows a de-rating being recovered from rather than a crowded trade being joined. Analyst recommendation trend improving, 66.7% bullish with strong buys going 6 to 7 month over month. Insiders effectively inactive: one $585,480 sale in six months and no open-market buys, which is neutral rather than negative.

recommendations.thesis: CVS reported Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.09 against a $1.667 consensus (+25.4%, the third consecutive beat above 15%), raised FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to at least $8.20 from $7.90-8.10, raised operating cash flow guidance to at least $15.5B from at least $11.5B, guided 2027 adjusted EPS to at least $8.65, and announced a tax-free split into two investment-grade companies — and the stock closed down 12.5% at 79.96, which is 9.25x that 2027 floor. The operating result and the price moved in opposite directions, so the de-rating is the market pricing PBM and drug-pricing legislative risk onto Caremark after the Democratic midterm sweep, not pricing the earnings. This is taken as a long-term accumulation rather than a swing because the downside is a valuation floor, not a level a stop can defend: the 2026-10-16 swing position in this name was gapped straight through its 85.40 stop on this very print.
recommendations.key_risk: The Democratic sweep makes PBM reform legislation materially more likely, and Caremark sits inside the Health Services segment management has already guided to a 2027 trough — a statutory change to PBM rebate economics would hit the highest-margin piece of the company and is the one risk no operating beat answers. Invalidation: PBM rebate reform enacted, the $8.65 2027 adjusted EPS floor withdrawn or cut when formal guidance lands on the February 2027 Q4 call, Health Services 2027 adjusted operating income guided below the $7B management called the trough, or the separation abandoned.
recommendations.counter_argument: The strongest case against is positioning rather than fundamentals: insiders sold $359.0M across nine transactions in the last six months with zero open-market purchases, and the stock sits roughly 12% below both its SMA20 (90.37) and SMA50 (90.82), so the accumulation is being started against the trend and against what the people inside the company did with their own shares. A second count against: the split does not complete until H1 2028, which is a long time to hold a thesis whose main re-rating catalyst is that distant. Red team, three more counts against. First, the thesis asserts that the 12.5% fall priced PBM legislative risk rather than the quarter, and research listed that as one of two unverified candidate explanations — the other being that the release carried no 2027 outlook where one was expected — and never settled which. The cause of the move was not established, which is the same standard that kept MRNA out of this report. Second, the 112.45 target is 13x against a stock at 9.25x, so most of the return is the multiple re-rating, and that requires the overhang `key_risk` calls the one risk no operating beat answers to resolve: at an unchanged 9.25x the $8.65 2027 floor is worth about $80, which is where the stock already trades, so the earnings growth alone pays nothing from here. Third, the tax-free split completes H1 2028, so a 13x multiple on consolidated $8.65 EPS is being applied to earnings that will by then sit in two separately-rated companies rather than in the share being bought today.

evidence.detail: Read the Q3 2026 release filed as Exhibit 99.1 to the 2026-11-04 8-K: adjusted EPS $2.09 vs $1.60, revenue $108.399B +5.4%, consolidated adjusted operating income $4,194M +21.2%, Health Care Benefits MBR 91.3% vs 92.8% (-150bps) with segment adjusted operating income $912M vs $314M, and FY26 adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $8.20 with operating cash flow raised to at least $15.5B from at least $11.5B.

Target is 13x the 2027 adjusted EPS floor of $8.65 given on the Q3 call = $112.45. 13x is defensible rather than heroic: the stock printed 110.68 inside the last 150 sessions on lower guidance, 13x forward is below the S&P multiple, and the $8.65 floor explicitly assumes no EPS accretion from the buyback resuming in Q4 2026 against $35B of deployable capital. The bear case is $66 — roughly 8.2x a flat, no-growth $8.00, below the 52-week low of 69.51 — giving reward-to-risk of 33.45/13.00 = 2.57 against the 2.5 long-term floor.

The bear case is that Health Services earnings keep eroding. Management put a number on it instead of asserting it away: Health Services adjusted operating income is guided to at least $7B in 2027 and named as the trough, with 340B declining y/y but largely stabilizing by the end of 2027 and now a smaller share of segment earnings. Separately, commercial premium revenue fell 16.9% because CVS has already exited the individual exchange business, so the ACA subsidy-cliff exposure that sits on peers is not on this balance sheet.

The position filled at 262.00 on 2026-10-12 and trades 303.99 (+21.0%), so a stop that protects profit sits ABOVE the entry of record, which this schema cannot express: validate_report.py's direction check requires the downside to be below the entry for a buy, and its stop-distance check measures from the fill and reads 1.46 ATR. Measured from the live price, 278.00 is 2.37 ATR below 303.99 and sits just under both the SMA20 (281.68) and SMA50 (279.05), which is where it belongs. Phase 2d's demotion was therefore certain, and it would have published a note reading as a rejection for a stop too tight; the number is recorded here instead. Two consequences the report did not state. (1) A stop amendment reaches state/open_positions.json only through `recommendations`, so the tracker will keep grading this position with no stop and the Performance tab will understate the protection actually in place — that is a tooling gap, not a change of mind. (2) From 303.99 the remaining trade is 35.77 of upside to 339.76 against 25.99 of risk to 278.00, which is 1.38:1 at a 42% break-even against the 45% win probability claimed. Running the whole position at a target 7.09 ATR away is close to a coin flip from here, so trim into strength rather than holding all of it to 339.76. The 262.00 entry stays as the truth: a filled position can have its exits amended, never its entry.
